title: 1.2 Billion People Use AI Every Week. Almost None Own It.
scaffold_note: Decision scaffold for the FROM-SCRATCH rebuild of soa-01, opened 2026-10-26 (JOB REBUILD-SOA01-1) under the owner's rebuild order of the same day. Phase 2 (2026-10-26) decides the architecture: role, story structure, hook form, style direction, delivery structure, end referral and scene form. Nothing here is copied as settled from the first draft (branch video/soa-01); where a value agrees with the first draft's record, the rationale says why it survives re-derivation.

objective.value: Show 1.2 billion weekly users rent AI access while owning none of the layer around it.
objective.rationale: The piece exists to make one number testify about ownership. The first draft's catalogue objective (16 words, recorded as GROUNDED in its script record) survives re-derivation unchanged: the fact it names (1.2B weekly users) is still the lane's load-bearing fact, and the rent/own gap is still the Academy's prescription read against it. Adopted because the reasoning re-checks out in this branch, not because the first draft carried it.
objective.source: archer reasoning (this branch, 2026-10-26), re-derived from files/short-soa01-billion-script.md
objective.record: files/short-soa01-billion-script.md — 'Objective (catalogue, GROUNDED, 16 words)'; canon.md §1–2 (the harness is where ownership lives)

message.value: Adoption is total. Ownership is zero. (Viewer restatement: 'Over a billion people now use AI every week — through a chat box they rent, keeping nothing of the layer around it.')
message.rationale: One message, two clauses: the scale of adoption and the absence of ownership, stated as a pair so the viewer can hold both in one breath. The essence line is the piece's own closing line (L6) — the message and the payoff are the same sentence, which is what makes the short quotable. The viewer restatement is kept because it translates the essence into the viewer's own situation (a chat box THEY rent).
message.source: archer reasoning (this branch, 2026-10-26), from the first draft's script record (essence + viewer restatement, 2026-10-22)

audience.value: The renters themselves: people who use AI every week through a chat box they do not own — the very users the 1.2B statistic counts. Secondarily, the AI-curious public who read adoption numbers as good news and have never asked who owns the layer. The misconception the piece corrects: 'I use ChatGPT every week, so the AI setup is mine — my instructions, my memory, my files belong to me.' In fact all of it lives on the provider's terms and vanishes when the tab closes.
audience.rationale: Decided by reasoning from the piece's own evidence, since the first draft's record never named an audience (its board phase-0 check stood pending — the one open scaffold field the first draft carried to its end). The evidence: (1) the closing bridge card speaks to the renter in the second person — 'Renters can become owners.' — a conversion appeal that only makes sense addressed to renters; (2) L5 explains the gap 'in doctrine language a newcomer can hold' (script record's own words), i.e. addressed to someone inside the chat box, not to builders; (3) the lane's phase-0 studies write for the general public encountering an adoption statistic (SOA-02's Pew brief addresses U.S. adults at large); (4) the funnel design — bridge to the Toaster long-form — presumes a viewer who rents today and could own tomorrow. Confidence: reasoning-grade, not measurement-grade; the residual is named in decisions/randomness-register.md.
audience.source: archer reasoning (this branch, 2026-10-26) — the removal mechanism for the first draft's standing OPEN
audience.record: files/short-soa01-billion-script.md (L5 intent; bridge card text) + files/short-soa02-half-america-phase0.md (lane audience pattern) + first-draft metadata.json fields.audience (the OPEN this decision removes)

role.value: APPLY — the Academy ownership doctrine applied to one dated fact. This lane reports and applies; it does not INTRODUCE the doctrine (that is the Toaster song's and Lesson 1's work).
role.rationale: The lane's division of labour is what keeps a 34-second report honest: soa-01 may presume the doctrine exists and spend all of its seconds applying it to this week's number, instead of re-teaching two-part doctrine (canon §1) in miniature. The first draft recorded the same role (its H5 record) after its own re-audit; re-derived here from the funnel structure itself — the bridge sends the viewer to the INTRODUCE piece, which only makes sense if this piece is the APPLY step.

story_structure.value: Dated-fact report form, six beats: dateline (L1) → the number (L2) → habit made visceral (L3) → the turn, 'the part nobody counts' (L4) → mechanism, the chat box as the thinnest harness (L5) → payoff: return & name, ADOPTION TOTAL / OWNERSHIP ZERO (L6) → silent bridge card. The question the video answers: 'How many people use AI every week — and how many of them own any of the layer they use it through?' The first half is answered by the fact (L2–L3); the second half is the turn and the payoff (L4–L6).
story_structure.rationale: The payoff schedule is the structure's spine: number first (so scale is felt before it is judged), habit second (so the number becomes behaviour, not trivia), the turn planted at L4 — late enough that the viewer has something to lose, early enough that the mechanism and the payoff still fit. A question-led restructure was weighed against this form in the transcript consolidation (phase 3, Candidate B) and rejected there; the structure decided here is the report form because the lane IS a report — its contract with the viewer is a dateline and a number, not a lesson.
story_structure.record: files/short-soa01-billion-script.md — 'Payoff schedule (H4)'; transcript/consolidation.md (phase 3) for the Candidate B weighing

hook_form.value: The number itself is the hook: 1.2 billion, huge on screen with its date and source, arriving at L2 (4.86 s) immediately after the lane's dateline opening (L1). The dateline is the lane's standing frame, not a hook substitute — the hook is the statistic.
hook_form.rationale: A dated-fact lane hooks with its fact or it hooks with nothing. The first draft's record (W-02) named the same hook; it survives because the reasoning is structural, not habitual: the number is the only element of the piece a cold viewer cannot scroll past without a reaction, and it is also the piece's evidence — hook and proof in one object. The 2.66 s dateline before it is the lane's report signature and costs less than the credibility the dateline buys.
hook_form.record: files/short-soa01-billion-script.md — Visual template ('W-02 hook = the number itself') + L1 intent

style_direction.value: MOTION GRAPHICS + 2D GRAPHICS (a mix of two of the 14 catalogue styles, both in the owner's starting set): flat graphic compartments carry the argument — the dot-crowd counter that multiplies toward 1.2B, the crowd greying at the turn until a handful of dots stay lit ('the owners'), the chat-box compartment with its three chips (instructions / memory / files), and the split-screen payoff (TOTAL ADOPTION / ZERO OWNERSHIP) — while word animation in the picture's empty lower band carries the narration's emphases per word. Cinematic typography is NOT this piece's decided style: it exists for this piece only as an experiment specimen (exp-02, lines 1–3) whose lane-level verdict is the owner's, still open; this branch does not pre-judge it.
style_direction.rationale: Discussion, as the style law requires. The piece's content is a statistic and a distinction (rent vs own); both are countable, divisible things, and motion-graphics compartments are the menu's native language for countable things — a crowd of dots can BE 1.2 billion in a way type alone cannot, and a crowd greying out can BE the turn. 2D flat graphics supply the compartment art (crowd, chat box, split screen) at the lane's fast production tier. Cinematic typography (the catalogue's Kinetic Typography; the owner's term) was genuinely weighed: the exp-02 specimen proves type alone can monumentalize the number and land L3's correction as a scale reversal — but it cannot draw the mechanism (a chat box with three named contents) or the owner handful inside the crowd, and adopting it here would spend the owner's open lane verdict (#79) without his word. Whiteboard and the A59 cutout grammar were considered and set aside for this piece: whiteboard's hand-drawn pace fights the report register, and per-word/per-object A59 treatment is the Word Definitions lane's adopted direction, not this lane's. The delivered first-draft build embodies exactly this motion-graphics + 2D mix; the decision is recorded here as this branch's own, with the specimen question left open in the randomness register.
style_direction.source: archer reasoning (this branch, 2026-10-26), from the piece's record + the owner's style rulings (#77 menu + starting set; #79 open)
style_direction.record: files/a59-motion-brief.md — STYLE MENU RULING (#77) + the 14-style catalogue; first-draft package experiments/exp-02/EXPERIMENT.md (the cinematic specimen, cited as evidence, not adopted)

delivery_structure.value: Line-delivered report at contiguous windows — no inter-line silence gaps are built into the narration: dateline (L1, 2.20–4.86 s) → number statement (L2, 4.86–7.68 s) → repetition-with-emphasis restatement (L3, 7.68–12.64 s: 'Not tried it once. Used it — this week.') → the turn (L4, 12.64–16.46 s) → mechanism, the longest line (L5, 16.46–23.98 s) → three-clause aphoristic close (L6, 23.98–28.006 s) → ONE designed silence (0.827 s) → silent bridge card (28.833–30.848 s, bed only) → bed-only outro to 34.348 s. Words arrive in phrases of ≤3 words at the spoken moment, in two alternating lower bands; a completed phrase HOLDS while the next reveals and clears when the phrase after next starts (C-05). Embodied as a measured pause map in phase 3 (transcript/delivery.md).
delivery_structure.rationale: The pattern is decided here; its sizes are measured, not asserted — phase 3's pause map derives every joint from the settled line windows and assigns each a function. Contiguity is itself the decision: a wire-report register does not breathe between facts; the single designed silence is spent where suspension pays — after the aphorism, before the ask. The first draft's finishing pass ratified the same delivered pattern from its windows; this branch adopts the pattern by the same reasoning and re-derives the map from the same windows.
delivery_structure.record: transcript/delivery.md (phase 3 — the pause map) + transcript/transcript.md (the settled windows)

end_referral.value: Silent bridge card after the L6 close (28.833–30.848 s): NEXT → 'Renters can become owners.' → toaster symbol → 'WHO OWNS THE TOASTER?' → 'the song that asks who owns the layer' → 'tap to watch →'. Target: the funnel long-form 'Who Owns the Toaster?' (fg2cV8sh3kY) on the flagship channel. Navigation load: the card's 2.015 s is 5.9% of the piece — inside the ≤10% navigation budget.
end_referral.rationale: The bridge is where the APPLY role cashes out: the piece has made a renter feel the gap; the card offers the doctrine piece that fills it, in the renter's own terms ('Renters can become owners.'). It is silent and bed-only so the aphorism's close is not talked over, and its text was built as a recorded decision in the first draft (H6, after standing RANDOM-ABSENT) — adopted here because its wording follows from this branch's decided audience: it speaks to exactly the viewer phase 1 named.
end_referral.record: files/short-soa01-billion-script.md — 'End referral (H6)'; first-draft scene DEC record DR-BRIDGE

scene_decomposition.value: The scene is ONE self-contained HTML file (H-01: the MP4 renders from this file alone), decomposed as a compartment inventory — a named home for every visual beat: (1) container compartment: intro, outro, series header; (2) six per-line compartments (dateline / number / habit-crowd / turn-crowd / chat box / payoff split); (3) the bridge compartment; (4) the word-animation layer; (5) the audio compartment; (6) the in-page decision-record layer; (7) player chrome. No physical split into separate HTML/CSS/JS files: the single-file form is itself the decision. Embodied and enumerated element-by-element in phase 4 (scene/scene.json).
scene_decomposition.rationale: Compartmentalization is the owner's standing demand — every visual detail gets a home so no element is anonymous. The inventory decided here follows the story structure one-for-one (each beat its compartment), which is what makes the scene editable beat by beat in phase 7. The first draft's finishing record enumerated the same compartments from its shipped file; this branch decides the inventory from the architecture first, then verifies the extracted scene against it in phase 4 — the order is the difference.
scene_decomposition.record: scene/scene.json (phase 4 — the verified inventory) + first-draft metadata.json fields.scene_decomposition (corroboration)
